diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
The OpenSearch domain `:resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch` is provisioned into a VPC (`vpc_options`, via `:module.aws_vpc`), and the AWS service-linked role (`:resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch`, gated on `var.create_iam_service_linked_role`) is created in the same configuration. The `aws_elasticsearch_domain` documentation explicitly states that VPC-based domains require the `AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService` service-linked role to exist before domain creation, and that `depends_on` must be used when the role is created alongside the domain. Without this ordering, first-time `apply` can fail with the domain returning an access-denied/error because the service-linked role does not yet exist. No attribute of the domain references the role, and no `depends_on` expresses this ordering, so the dependency is missing.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch is deployed inside a VPC (it references module.aws_vpc and aws_security_group.opensearch_access), but it has no dependency on aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch. AWS requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to exist before a domain with vpc_options can be created; on the first apply (or whenever var.create_iam_service_linked_role is true and the role is being created in the same run) the domain creation will fail because no dependency orders the role ahead of the domain. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch] to the domain resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
The VPC-based OpenSearch/Elasticsearch domain (":resource.aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch") uses vpc_options, which requires the AWSServiceRoleForAmazonElasticsearchService service-linked role to exist before the domain can be created. The project declares ":resource.aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch" (gated by var.create_iam_service_linked_role) for exactly this purpose, but the domain has no dependency on it — neither an attribute reference nor an explicit depends_on. If var.create_iam_service_linked_role is true, both resources will be created in parallel and the domain creation can fail with a "no service-linked role" API error on first apply. The provider documentation explicitly requires depends_on for this case (service-linked roles cannot be referenced via a data dependency), so a bare depends_on is the correct fix.
